question: What does the Comfort Club membership include?
html:
What the Comfort Club includes

We don't yet have the Comfort Club's benefits in our source material, so we can't list what it covers. Membership appears in our planning only as a member count and a growth target. Neither describes tune-ups, discounts or priority service.

What our data does show

  • Membership is in our growth plan, but every figure is an assumption, not a reported number (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • The plan counts membership growth, along with AI answering and booking, as a driver of +10-12% organic growth in the first 12 months, est. (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • The base being served is old and mostly owner-occupied. Across the core counties, 45-64% of homes were built before 1980, and owner-occupancy runs 63-82% (Punctual Pros market profile).
  • About 241k core Pennsylvania households still heat with fuel oil or propane (Punctual Pros market profile). Any plan terms for those homes are not in our data.

Data that would answer this

  • The current member agreement and terms for each trade: plumbing, HVAC and electrical.
  • The visit schedule, discount rates, priority-scheduling rules and any repair guarantees.
  • Pricing by tier, and whether terms differ between the Pennsylvania and New Jersey (Horvath) territories.
  • Any brand-level membership standards set by Authority Brands for One Hour, Ben Franklin and Mister Sparky locations.

Until we have those, call the local team for current plan details. Don't rely on a generic description.

A clearly published membership offer turns one-off repair calls in an old housing stock into recurring, schedulable revenue. The growth plan assumes members will grow from about 6,500 to 32,000 in three years, est.

Next actions for the operating team

  1. Pull the current membership agreement and price sheet for each trade and each state. Publish an approved summary for the website.
  2. Confirm the actual active member count against the 6,500 estimate. Record the source and date.
  3. Check whether oil and propane heating homes need separate plan terms. Document them if so.
  4. Align the website wording with any Authority Brands membership standards before launch.

# What the Comfort Club includes

We don't yet have the Comfort Club's benefits in our source material, so we can't list what it covers. Membership appears in our planning only as a member count and a growth target. Neither describes tune-ups, discounts or priority service.

## What our data does show

- Membership is in our growth plan, but every figure is an assumption, not a reported number (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- The plan counts membership growth, along with AI answering and booking, as a driver of +10-12% organic growth in the first 12 months, est. (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- The base being served is old and mostly owner-occupied. Across the core counties, 45-64% of homes were built before 1980, and owner-occupancy runs 63-82% (Punctual Pros market profile).
- About 241k core Pennsylvania households still heat with fuel oil or propane (Punctual Pros market profile). Any plan terms for those homes are not in our data.

| Point in plan | Members (est.) | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Month 0 (Oct 2026) | 6,500 | ~0.9% of core owner-occupied units, assumed |
| Month 12 | 11,000 | Phase 1 complete, assumed |
| Month 24 | 20,000 | Assumed |
| Month 36 | 32,000 | Assumed |

(Punctual Pros nationwide plan)

## Data that would answer this

- The current member agreement and terms for each trade: plumbing, HVAC and electrical.
- The visit schedule, discount rates, priority-scheduling rules and any repair guarantees.
- Pricing by tier, and whether terms differ between the Pennsylvania and New Jersey (Horvath) territories.
- Any brand-level membership standards set by Authority Brands for One Hour, Ben Franklin and Mister Sparky locations.

Until we have those, call the local team for current plan details. Don't rely on a generic description.

A clearly published membership offer turns one-off repair calls in an old housing stock into recurring, schedulable revenue. The growth plan assumes members will grow from about 6,500 to 32,000 in three years, est.

## Next actions for the operating team

1. Pull the current membership agreement and price sheet for each trade and each state. Publish an approved summary for the website.
2. Confirm the actual active member count against the 6,500 estimate. Record the source and date.
3. Check whether oil and propane heating homes need separate plan terms. Document them if so.
4. Align the website wording with any Authority Brands membership standards before launch.
